content.text:
I submitted index 1 (Fe 0.83 / Sb 0.17) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of the three I measured, at 0.544%.

| Index | Fe fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 0.49 | 0.0056 |
| 5 | 0.74 | 0.229 |
| 1 | 0.83 | 0.544 |

- **1:1 composition:** The models backed the Fe:Sb 1:1 compound FeSbO₄: it came out stable, with a predicted band gap of 2.08 eV, below the 2.7 eV photon energy. It still gave almost no EQE, so the band gap prediction did not reflect real performance.
- **Fe-rich side:** EQE went up steeply as Fe increased. I expect those films are mostly hematite (Fe₂O₃) with some Sb, but I used none of the 5 XRD scans, so I haven't confirmed which phases are there.
- **Band gap predictions:** The model's hematite gap ranged from 0.8 to 2.8 eV depending on the calculation method, so it didn't help choose between compositions.

EQE was still rising at the Fe-rich end, so index 0 (Fe 0.85) could be as good or slightly better. The 3 EQE measurements ran out before I could test it.
